title: Gyeran Mari Korean Rolled Omelette

description: Gyeran Mari is a beloved Korean rolled omelette, a delightful side dish or breakfast item known for its soft, fluffy texture and vibrant layers. This comforting egg dish is typically made by rolling thin layers of seasoned egg mixture, often with finely chopped vegetables, into a beautiful cylinder. Enjoy this versatile and delicious Korean staple at any time of day.

ingredients.notes: optional, for a hint of sweetness

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Dice the carrot and chop the green onions very finely. This ensures they cook evenly within the omelette layers and do not tear the delicate egg while rolling. Set aside.

instructions.title: Whisk the Egg Mixture
instructions.text: In a medium bowl, whisk the large eggs until they are well combined and slightly frothy. Stir in the finely diced carrots, chopped green onions, salt, and the optional sugar. Add the water or milk to the mixture, which helps create a softer, fluffier texture for the omelette.

instructions.title: Heat and Prepare the Pan
instructions.text: Lightly oil a non-stick rectangular or round pan (preferably an 8-inch square or 10-inch round pan works best for rolling) over medium-low heat. It is crucial to use low heat to cook the omelette slowly and prevent burning. Wipe any excess oil with a paper towel, leaving just a thin, even film.

instructions.title: Pour the First Layer
instructions.text: Pour about 1/4 to 1/3 of the egg mixture into the hot pan, tilting the pan to form a thin, even layer that covers the bottom. Let it cook undisturbed until the bottom is set and lightly golden, but the top is still slightly wet and pliable. This partial setting is key for successful rolling.

instructions.title: Begin Rolling the Omelette
instructions.text: When the egg layer is mostly set but still flexible, gently start rolling the omelette from one side of the pan towards the other using a spatula. Roll it tightly but carefully. Once rolled, push the formed omelette to one side of the pan, leaving about two-thirds of the pan empty.

instructions.title: Add Subsequent Layers
instructions.text: Lightly re-oil the empty part of the pan if needed. Pour another 1/4 to 1/3 of the egg mixture into the empty space, making sure some of the new mixture flows underneath the rolled omelette. Cook until this new layer is mostly set but still slightly wet on top.

instructions.title: Continue Rolling and Cooking
instructions.text: Once the new layer is mostly set, continue rolling the existing omelette over the fresh egg layer, incorporating it into the growing roll. Repeat steps 6 and 7 until all the egg mixture is used, creating a thick, multi-layered omelette roll. Once fully rolled, cook for another 1-2 minutes, gently pressing all sides with the spatula to ensure it is cooked through and holds its shape.

instructions.title: Slice and Serve
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the finished Gyeran Mari to a cutting board. Let it cool slightly for a few minutes; this helps it firm up and makes slicing easier. Using a sharp knife, slice the rolled omelette into 1-inch thick pieces. Serve warm as a side dish for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, often with rice and other Korean banchan.

tips: For perfectly even layers, use a very low heat and ensure each layer is mostly set but still slightly wet before rolling. This prevents cracking and helps the layers adhere.

Finely dicing vegetables like carrots and green onions is crucial. Larger pieces can tear the delicate egg layers, making it difficult to roll neatly. You can also add finely minced ham or seaweed for variation.
Let the Gyeran Mari cool for a few minutes on a cutting board before slicing. This allows the omelette to firm up, resulting in cleaner, more defined slices.
